# Hair Salon TikTok Strategy: Before and After Videos

Part of the guide: [Hair Salon & Barbershop Social Media & Meta Ads](https://datalatte.pro/guides/salon-social)

May 19, 2026·Nataliia Rumiantsewa· 7 min read [All posts](https://datalatte.pro/blog)

On this page▼

A hair salon should post short before-and-after videos from a TikTok Business account, with the client's written consent, the service and city in the caption, and a booking link in the profile. Boost the posts that already perform with Spark Ads, which TikTok describes as a format that promotes existing organic posts. Pew's 2026 survey found 65% of US adults aged 18 to 29 and 45% of those aged 30 to 49 use TikTok, so the audience is there.

No source checked here publishes how many bookings a transformation video brings, so this page gives none. It covers setup, budget minimums, disclosure rules and the numbers to watch.

See Sources at the end of the article. Cards marked Assumption are examples, not results.

## Why Do Before-and-After Videos Suit a Salon?

The result is visual, and the change happens in seconds. A viewer sees the starting point, the work and the outcome without reading anything. That makes the format easy to understand with the sound off and gives the viewer a reason to watch to the end.

It also gives a salon proof without claims. Show the real hair, the service name and the approximate time it took. Avoid editing that changes the colour or length, because the client will compare the video with the result in the chair. Our guide on [before-and-after photos, legal and converting](https://datalatte.pro/blog/hair-salon-before-after-photos-legal-and-converting) covers consent in more detail.

## How Do You Set Up the Account?

TikTok advises anyone promoting a business to use a Business Account. Business Accounts can put a website link on the profile, so use your booking page. TikTok also notes they only have access to Commercial Sounds, the library cleared for commercial use, instead of the wider music library.

Fill the profile: salon name, city, hours and what you do, such as colour, cuts and extensions. Pin your three best transformations. Then post consistently for a few weeks before you judge. For ideas on formats beyond this one, see [TikTok marketing for hair salons](https://datalatte.pro/blog/tiktok-marketing-for-hair-salons).

Want a free review of your Google presence?

Send your business name. I reply with a short action plan within 48 hours.

[Get my free audit](https://datalatte.pro/free-audit)

## What Rules Apply to Client Videos?

Get written permission before you post a client's face or hair. If you give a free or discounted service in return for a video, the FTC says that counts as a material connection and must be disclosed clearly. Its guidance says terms like "ad" or "sponsored" are generally enough, vague shorthand like "collab" is not, and the disclosure should be in the video itself, not only the description.

Keep a simple form: name, date, what may be posted and where, and how to withdraw consent. This protects you if a client later changes their mind.

## How Do You Structure a Transformation Video?

A repeatable structure saves time:

1.  First second: the "before" shot with a one-line text overlay, such as "Level 5 to blonde".
2.  Middle: two or three quick process shots.
3.  End: the "after" from the same angle and light as the "before".
4.  Caption: the service, the city and how to book.

Film in the same spot with the same light. Mention the real time the service took. If the result took two sessions, say so.

## When Should You Pay to Boost a Video?

After a video has performed well organically. TikTok says Spark Ads let you promote your own posts and credit the views, likes and follows to the original post. Ads Manager requires a daily budget above $20 for an ad group and above $50 for a campaign, and a lifetime ad group budget equal to days times that minimum, so a 31-day run needs at least $620.

The example is an **assumption**: a salon boosts its best video for 7 days at the $20 ad group minimum, so $140 in total. It sets a booking link and a promo code and counts bookings that use the code. If three bookings use the code, the cost per booking is about $47 before the client's later visits. The three bookings are invented for the arithmetic, not a forecast.

## Which Numbers Should You Watch?

TikTok defines a 6-second view as a play lasting at least 6 seconds or the full video if shorter, and a 100% view as watched to the end, excluding replays. Compare these with total views. A video with many plays but few 6-second views has a weak first moment. Also count profile link clicks and bookings with your code.

See [video marketing for salons](https://datalatte.pro/blog/video-marketing-for-salons-reels-tiktok-guide) for reusing clips on Instagram, and [TikTok ads for hair salons](https://datalatte.pro/blog/tiktok-ads-for-hair-salons) for paid setup.

## FAQ

### Do I need a Business Account for my salon?

TikTok recommends it for anyone promoting a business. You get a website link on the profile but only Commercial Sounds.

### Can I post a client's before-and-after without asking?

No. Get written consent. If you gave a discount or free service in return, disclose it clearly in the video.

### How much does it cost to boost a video?

TikTok's minimums are above $20 a day for an ad group and above $50 for a campaign. Click and view prices are not published as averages here.

### How many videos should I post?

No source gives an exact number. Pick a rate you can keep for 8 to 12 weeks, then compare results.

### What are Spark Ads?

A format that promotes an existing organic post, with engagement credited to the original post.

## Sources

### [What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-2)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### [Work Environment](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-3)

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists work mostly in barbershops or salons. Most are full time, although part-time work is common. Work schedules may vary and often include evenings and weekends.

### [How to Become a Barber, Hairstylist, or Cosmetologist](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-4)

All states require barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists to be licensed. To qualify for a license, candidates typically must graduate from a state-approved barber or cosmetology program and pass an exam.

### [Pay](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-5)

The median hourly wage for barbers was $18.37 in May 2025.

The median hourly wage for hairdressers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists was $17.21 in May 2025.

### [Job Outlook](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-6)

Overall employment of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists is projected to grow 7 percent from 2025 to 2035, much faster than the average for all occupations.

About 80,300 openings for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists are projected each year, on average, over the decade. Many of those openings are expected to result from the need to replace workers who transfer to different occupations or exit the labor force, such as to retire.

### [State & Area Data](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-7)

Explore resources for employment and wages by state and area for barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists.

### [Similar Occupations](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-8)

Compare the job duties, education, job growth, and pay of barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists with similar occupations.

### [More Information, Including Links to O*NET](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#tab-9)

Learn more about barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists by visiting additional resources, including O*NET, a source on key characteristics of workers and occupations.

## What Barbers, Hairstylists, and Cosmetologists Do[About this section](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/personal-care-and-service/barbers-hairstylists-and-cosmetologists.htm#TB_inline?height=325&width=325&inlineId=about-what-they-do)

![Image 1: Barbers, hairdressers, and cosmetologists](https://www.bls.gov/ooh/images/2711.jpg)

Hairstylists provide hair styling and beauty services.

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide haircutting, hairstyling, and other services related to personal appearance.

### Duties

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists typically do the following:

*   Inspect and analyze hair, scalp, and skin to recommend services or treatment
*   Discuss hairstyle options
*   Shampoo, color, lighten, and condition hair
*   Chemically change hair texture
*   Cut, dry, and style hair
*   Trim facial hair
*   Receive payments from client
*   Clean and disinfect all tools and work areas

Barbers, hairstylists, and cosmetologists provide hair and other services to enhance clients’ appearance. Common tools may include combs and hairbrushes, clippers and scissors, straight razors, blow dryers, and curling and flat irons. They also may keep records of products used and services provided to clients, such as hair color, hair treatment, and clipper setting.

Many Americans use social media to connect with one another, engage with news content, share information and entertain themselves. Explore the patterns and trends shaping the social media landscape.

About this research

This fact sheet is the latest in our long-running series on technology adoption in the United States. For more than a decade, we’ve surveyed Americans to understand which social media platforms they use.

#### Why did we do this?

Pew Research Center does research to inform the public, journalists and decision-makers. This research builds on our past work [studying social media platforms Americans use](https://www.pewresearch.org/topic/internet-technology/platforms-services/social-media/).

[Learn more about Pew Research Center](https://www.pewresearch.org/about/).

#### [](https://www.pewresearch.org/topic/internet-technology/platforms-services/social-media/)How did we do this?

This analysis is based on findings from the National Public Opinion Reference Survey, a Center survey of 5,511 U.S. adults. We allowed people to respond online, by mail or by phone. The survey represents the views of all U.S. adults.

The survey was conducted Jan. 30-June 18, 2026. Its overall margin of error is plus or minus 1.8 percentage points.

This analysis also includes past data. The ways we’ve allowed people to respond to these surveys have evolved over the years, including in 2023 and again in 2024. For more on these shifts and how we approached them, read our [mobile](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/mobile/) and [broadband](https://www.pewresearch.org/internet/fact-sheet/internet-broadband/) fact sheets and [our Q&A](https://www.pewresearch.org/short-reads/2024/01/31/q-and-a-how-and-why-were-changing-the-way-we-study-tech-adoption/).

Here are the [questions used for this analysis](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_Questionnaire.pdf), the [topline](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_TOPLINE.pdf) and the [survey methodology](https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/10/PI_2026.10.19_NPORS-Internet-Fact-Sheets_Methodology.pdf).

# About A/B testing for Meta Ads

A/B testing enables you to compare two versions of an ad strategy by changing variables such as ad images, ad text, audience or placement. Each version is shown to a segment of your audience, ensuring nobody sees both, then the test determines which version performs best. Running an A/B test helps you decide which ad strategy to use.

Before you select a variable to test, choose a [hypothesis for your test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/2358258211160819). For example, you might hypothesize that a custom audience strategy will outperform an interest-based audience strategy for your business.

## How A/B testing works in Meta Ads Manager

To create an A/B test, you can either duplicate an existing campaign, ad set or ad and change a variable, or compare two existing campaigns or ad sets. If you choose to duplicate an existing campaign, your ad budget is also duplicated. Otherwise, your current ad budgets are used, which you can change in Meta Ads Manager at the ad set level. Use the same budget for both versions in a test to ensure a fair comparison. A/B testing can then measure the performance of each strategy on a cost per result basis or cost per conversion lift basis.

## When to use an A/B test for your Meta ads

We recommend A/B testing when you’re trying to measure changes to your advertising or quickly compare two strategies. We do not recommend testing informally, such as by turning ad sets or campaigns on and off manually. Informal testing can lead to inefficient ad delivery and unreliable test results. For example, A/B testing helps ensure your audiences will be evenly split and statistically comparable, while informal testing can lead to overlapping audiences.

You can [create an A/B test in Meta Ads Manager](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/355670925639619) or in the [**Experiments** tool](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/3506622486044209). Learn more about the [ways to create an A/B test](https://www.facebook.com/business/help/1159714227408868).
